$comment: R1947 — the analysis tool's TOPOLOGY section, written down once, in neutral
vocabulary, as the behaviour reference draws it.
WHY THIS SECTION IS BEING BUILT NOW, and what makes it different from the
four that came before it. Every earlier section closed a gap against the
SCOPE reference — the first-stage screen mockup — whose rail this build
reproduces seat for seat. This one does not: the mockup draws this seat
LOCKED, booked under requirement 12, and this build locked it the same way
for 219 rounds. What the mockup cannot see is that the BEHAVIOUR reference
— the working prototype, a superset of it — BUILDS this section: its rail
moves here like any other seat, a section-selected predicate names it, and
it has a full view of its own.
R1946 measured that divergence and made it a list (`second_phase_owed` in
docs/analyzer-rail-spec.json). This file is what pays the first entry off.
So the seat opening here is NOT a first-stage reproduction gap closing; it
is the second stage arriving, which the owner's 2026-08-19 order asks for
in exactly this position: reproduce the first stage, then improve past it.
The rail pin records the divergence rather than hiding it.
EXTRACTION. The reference is not in this repository and must not be. Its
topology view is three panes: a filter rail, a graph, and an inspector.
Measured at the command on 2026-09-01: a 238-wide filter column with four
labelled groups, a graph column whose 46-high header carries the section
title, the layout in force, a live mark and a fit control, and a 308-wide
inspector with a headline, a status line, a four-tile grid, a key list and
two actions. The node population is six peers around one router.
VOCABULARY. The reference's product, protocol and resource words are
replaced by the words this tree already uses for them — the key patterns
are `hello-key-patterns`'s own, and the router is `R-01` as the sibling
sections name it. Structure and behaviour are what is reproduced.
THE TWO HALVES, as in every sibling pin: `canon` is what the reference
draws. `owed` is where this build does not draw it yet, each entry saying
why. The gate asserts the difference between the painted surface and
`canon` is EXACTLY `owed`, so a new divergence fails and so does an owed
one that has been paid off without this file being told.
The left column, 238 wide. Four labelled groups under a heading that
states the observed population — the reference puts the count in the
heading rather than in the graph, so a reader knows what they are
looking at before it is drawn.
The middle column. A 46-high header, then the plot. The header's second
run states WHICH layout is in force, which is the reference's own
affordance for a control whose two buttons are in the other pane — the
graph says what it is showing rather than making a reader look away.
`canvas` is the plot as one surface. Its interior — a node's circle, a
link's line, a label — is not part of this roster on purpose: those are
a population that changes with the capture, and a specification that
enumerated them would be a copy of the data rather than of the screen.
What holds them is `painted.rs`'s own sweep, which asserts every
declared node is drawn and reaches its own inspector.
The right column, 308 wide. What the reference shows about the node a
reader picked: an identity block, a four-tile grid of measurements, the
key patterns observed on that node, and two actions.
★ `isolate` and `detach` are drawn and REFUSED here, which is this
tree's established treatment of a reference control that leads out of a
section nothing has built. The reference draws them live and answers a
later-stage toast; drawing them absent would lose the affordance and
drawing them live would promise a section that does not exist, so they
are present, disabled, and each states the requirement that books it —
the same shape `hello-key-patterns` uses for the action out of its own
section.
